settings.name_in_paper: Parallel/delayed GP bandit optimization, compact convex D ⊆ [0,l]^d, f sampled from known GP prior (Theorem 1, assumption 2)
unmapped: feedback mapping fb[t] with t - fb[t] <= B_delay for a known constant B_delay

settings.definition_quote: D ⊆ [0, l]^d is compact and convex, d ∈ N, l > 0. f is sampled from a known GP prior with known noise variance σn^2, and k(x, x') satisfies the following bound w.h.p. on the derivatives of GP sample paths f: for some constants a, b > 0, Pr{sup |∂f/∂xj| > L} ≤ a e^{-(L/b)^2}

settings.name_in_paper: Parallel/delayed GP bandit optimization, f with bounded RKHS norm (Theorem 1, assumption 3)
unmapped: feedback mapping fb[t] with t - fb[t] <= B_delay for a known constant B_delay
noise is a martingale difference sequence uniformly bounded by sigma_n (bounded, hence conditionally sub-Gaussian)
settings.definition_quote: D is arbitrary; f has RKHS norm ||f||_k ≤ M. The noise εt form an arbitrary martingale difference sequence (meaning that E[εt | ε1, ..., εt−1] = 0 for all t ∈ N), uniformly bounded by σn.

source.quote: Theorem 1. Let δ ∈ (0, 1). Suppose one of the following assumptions holds: 1. D is finite, f is sampled from a known GP prior with known noise variance σn^2, and αt = 2 log(|D|t^2 π^2/6δ). ... Then, the cumulative regret of GP-BUCB, using βt = exp(2C)α_fb[t], is bounded by O*(sqrt(T γT exp(2C)αT)) w.h.p. Precisely, Pr{RT ≤ C1 sqrt(T exp(2C)αT γT) + 2 ∀T ≥ 1} ≥ 1−δ where C1 = 8/log(1 + σn^{-2}).

results.notes: Probability over GP prior draw of f and noise; regret is sum of f(x*)-f(x_t). Holds for all T simultaneously. Compute: polynomial per round for finite D.

source.quote: Theorem 2. Suppose one of the conditions of Theorem 1 is satisfied. Further suppose the kernel and T init are as listed in Table 1. Fix δ > 0. Let RT be the regret of GP-BUCB, which ignores feedback for the first T init rounds. Then there exists a constant C' independent of B such that for any T ≥ 0, it holds with probability at least 1 − δ that RT ≤ C' RT^seq + 2||f||∞ T init, where C' takes the value shown in Table 1.
